source.title: A Dominant Diffuse Phase in the Sparse Autoencoder Phase Diagram

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests recovery of a known sparse synthetic dictionary with trained SAEs and finds a diffuse, poorly aligned regime rather than complete recovery or merging. This refines the claim that SAE features are complete units, but it does not test the original toy-network geometry directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own synthetic-dictionary recovery, alignment, and robustness results. Claims or results it cites from other studies are not recorded. It does not report pairwise angles among learned atoms, so the table's feature-alignment measures do not establish whether the learned directions are nearly orthogonal.
record.test_reason: The study trains vanilla ReLU+L1 SAEs on synthetic data built from a known 256-atom dictionary superposed in 64 dimensions. It measures whether the learned atoms recover that dictionary. Across 200 canonical fits and 3,300 minibatch fits it finds no full recovery and low alignment. This bears directly on whether dictionary features are complete, faithful units (V5), though only for synthetic sparse-coding data, not a trained network's activations. It does not train a toy network, so V1 geometry is untested. It does not study neurons, LLMs or multi-dimensional features (V2, V3, V4, V6).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially right. The authors also stress three further points. Zero merges occurred, even at full nesting. The diffuse regime is reached by every initialization, survives doubled training and minibatch Adam, and holds across the full 165-cell grid. Nesting fraction has little effect on alignment, but is confounded with child rarity. They conclude that near-perfect reconstruction is compatible with zero feature recovery.
record.recipe_differences: This is a controlled synthetic sparse-dictionary/SAE experiment, not a reproduction of the original toy-network setup. It varies nesting fraction, sparsity penalty, and dictionary size, and evaluates decoder-atom recovery, merging, and alignment under a specified trained SAE protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured alignment summaries vary with sparsity penalty and dictionary size: the five-cell lambda sweep at gamma=0.5 has an interior maximum at lambda=3 × 10^-3, and the matched-feature fraction rises from 0.001 to 0.036 when M doubles from 256 to 512 at fixed gamma=0.5 and lambda=10^-3. The paper reports little alignment effect across the measured gamma cells, but gamma jointly changes nesting dependence and child rarity. The minibatch optimizer and doubled training budget did not materially change the diffuse outcome at the tested peak cell.

fits_no_version.finding: Learned codes are 9.9-27.9x denser than the ground-truth codes, despite near-floor reconstruction loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trained vanilla L1 SAEs can reconstruct superposed sparse data near-perfectly with a diffuse, much denser code, so reconstruction does not certify feature recovery.

fits_no_version.finding: No atom meets the pairwise merge criterion in any fit, even at gamma=1 where every feature is nested. Theory predicts exact-coding minimizers merge nested features in the two-feature case.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trained amortized SAEs need not reach the merging minima predicted for the exact sparse-coding objective.

record.problems: Only 10 of 165 canonical full-batch grid cells were measured; the remaining cells are covered only by the explicitly off-protocol minibatch companion grid. One fixed dictionary and fixed datasets are used. Along gamma, nesting and child-frequency changes are confounded. The paper notes that the late loss trajectories are still changing slightly and that the longer-training probe applies to one selected cell, not every cell. The canonical results measure trained amortized SAEs, not global minimizers.
record.rows_left_out: Per-cell counts of features with cosine >= 0.90, density values, reconstruction losses, and split counts in Table 1 were omitted because the core feature-alignment and recovery results are already represented, and those additional measures do not independently test completeness of SAE features. The minibatch grid's per-cell matched-feature fractions and split counts in Figure 4 were not expanded into rows; the paper reports the grid-wide zero-recovery and zero-merge outcomes and the maximum matched-feature fraction of 0.046.

untested.parts: No toy network is trained. Superposition is imposed by the data generator (y=Φx), so the study gives no test of learned near-orthogonal geometry or a sparsity-dependent transition.
Neurons and capacity competition are not studied.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons are not studied.
No LLM activations are used, and there is no measure of feature spread across real neurons.

Untested: stability or canonicity of features across SAE variants (gated, top-k, Matryoshka), data draws or dictionary draws, and any SAE trained on real model activations. Only one fixed dictionary is used, with vanilla ReLU+L1 SAEs.
The ground-truth atoms are 1-D, and no comparison with multi-dimensional features is made.

missing.what: Probe B minibatch median best cosine of 0.739 (vs 0.727 canonical), with about 0.25 features per run above 0.95. This shows alignment is insensitive to optimizer.
Pooled individual matches: 44 of 200 runs have at least one matched feature, 215 assignments in total (0.42% of possible assignments).

record.verdict_notes: V5 is about SAE features as the units of a model's representation. This study tests SAE recovery on synthetic superposed sparse data with a known dictionary, not on activations of a trained network, so the verdicts are a ground-truth proxy for V5. The settings are deliberately dense (m/n=4, about 8 features active at once) and use a vanilla architecture without resampling, which the authors flag as possible reasons for the contrast with prior toy-SAE results. Only 10 of the 165 canonical cells were measured; the full grid is off-protocol minibatch. Matched fractions of 0.001 and 0.005 were reclassified as absent. Rows on merges were unlinked from V5. The study is a single-author preprint.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the original toy-network superposition geometry, near-orthogonality of overlapping directions, or a sparsity-dependent geometric transition.
Does not test whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by features competing for neuronal capacity or whether important features obtain dedicated neurons.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
Uses synthetic data, not LLM activations; it does not measure feature spread across LLM neurons or SAE recovery from LLMs.
Tests recovery of a known synthetic dictionary by the specified trained SAE, not whether SAE features are stable or canonical across models, datasets, or SAE variants.
Uses one-dimensional ground-truth dictionary atoms but does not compare one-dimensional with multidimensional feature representations.

relationships.condition: Vanilla ReLU+L1 SAEs on the MAIS-O43 synthetic dictionary (n=64, m=256), in the 10 canonical full-batch cells, the 2x-budget continuation, and the minibatch probe and 165-cell grid
relationships.reason: Full-dictionary recovery is 0/200 canonical fits, 0/20 at 400k updates and 0/3,300 minibatch fits. Matched fractions are at or near 0 in the M=256 cells (r1-r9, r21, r23, r24, r26).
relationships.display_finding: Full-dictionary recovery was 0 of 200 canonical fits, 0 of 20 at 400k updates and 0 of 3,300 minibatch fits, with matched fractions at or near 0 in the M=256 cells.

relationships.condition: Alignment as a function of sparsity penalty and dictionary size (gamma=0.5 lambda sweep; M=512 vs M=256)
relationships.reason: Atoms are only partly aligned (median best cosine 0.47-0.73). Alignment peaks at lambda=3e-3 (r16) and rises with M=512 (matched fraction 0.036, cosine 0.712; r10, r20), so the degree of recovery depends on SAE choices.
relationships.display_finding: Median best cosine was only 0.47–0.73; alignment peaked at lambda=3e-3 and was higher at M=512 than at M=256 (matched fraction 0.036, cosine 0.712).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Canonical full-batch SAE fits in the 10 measured synthetic-dictionary cells; also the minibatch companion-grid results
reader_labels.reason: The study finds no full-dictionary recovery in 200 canonical fits or 3,300 minibatch fits, with low matched-feature fractions in the measured cells (r1-r10, r21, r26). This challenges completeness of SAE recovery in these tested settings.
